artworks.title: Pentheus Torn by Maenads (House of the Vettii, Pompeii)
artworks.description: The triclinium fresco in the Casa dei Vettii freezes Euripides' climax: Pentheus, still in women's dress, torn limb from limb by Agave and the maenads. Roman wall-painting makes the Bacchae's sparagmos domestic decoration.

artworks.title: Death of Pentheus (Douris cup, Kimbell Art Museum)
artworks.description: Douris paints the Theban king already dismembered on an Attic red-figure cup — maenads wielding his limbs as trophies. The Kimbell kylix is among the earliest and clearest images of Pentheus' death.

artworks.title: Death of Pentheus (Louvre G445)
artworks.description: On this Attic red-figure lekanis lid in the Louvre, Agave and Ino tear Pentheus apart — the Bacchae's mother-murder rendered in clay. The vase keeps the Theban king's refusal of Dionysus as a visual warning.

artworks.title: Maenads Killing Pentheus (Meidias Painter, Kerameikos)
artworks.description: A Kerameikos hydria in the Meidias Painter's ornate style stages the sparagmos: maenads closing on Pentheus. Athenian luxury pottery makes the Bacchic killing a jewelled surface.

films.title: Dionysus in '69
films.description: De Palma and Schechner film The Performance Group's ritual Bacchae — Pentheus torn in a New York warehouse as living theatre bleeds into cinema.

films.title: The Bacchantes
films.description: Ferroni's peplum Bacchae casts Alberto Lupo as Pentheus against Pierre Brice's Dionysus — the Theban king's refusal dressed for Italian sword-and-sandal spectacle.

music.title: The Bassarids
music.description: Henze's Auden–Kallman Bacchae makes Pentheus the voice of rational order destroyed by Dionysus — sparagmos rewritten as modern opera at Salzburg.

popCulture.title: The Bacchae
popCulture.creator: Euripides
popCulture.description: Euripides' tragedy keeps Pentheus on every modern stage — the Theban king torn by maenads as the emblem of a city that refuses the god.
